export const meta = {
  name: 'review-pipeline-harness-bot-1-3',
  description: 'Read-only independent review + adversarial verification of the queue->builder->send pipeline test harness for bots 1 and 3',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Review', detail: '4 independent read-only reviewers, one per dimension' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial refutation of every finding, plus the lead candidate list' },
  ],
}

const R = 'C:\\Users\\NTD\\Desktop\\Bot Market Demo\\dich-nguoc\\khoi-phuc'

const CONTEXT = `
ROLE: Independent read-only reviewer of a test harness written by the project owner. The owner is restoring lost MQL5 source for their own MT5 bots ("bot 1" and "bot 3"); the original EX5 stays unchanged; only a private test MT5 is used with trading disabled, and every order-send call is replaced by supplied test data. Evaluate THE HARNESS (what it really checks). Do not propose changing protections, keys or the original EX5.

HARD RULES: Read-only. Use only Read / Grep / Glob. Do NOT run shell, Python, MT5 or anything that executes code. Do NOT create or modify files. Do not read the very large cases.json files; reason from the case generator functions instead. .bin files are binary: reason from the code that writes/reads them. Cite every claim as path:line using the line numbers that Read shows. If something cannot be verified from the files, say "unverified" and why; never guess. Keep proven defects separate from unverified limitations.

SYSTEM UNDER REVIEW (data flow):
1. prepare: kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh-bot-1-3.py cases() -> cases.bin.
2. mql5: a private MT5 runs Bot{N}PendingPipelineCheck.ex5, which runs the restored MQL5 queue -> pending builder -> filling -> send wrapper -> message code, with terminal APIs replaced by mocks in Bot{N}PipelineApi.mqh. It writes mql5-results.bin (per-case results) and api-fixtures.bin (every mocked API call with its arguments and the value it returned, plus builder before/after snapshots; event codes 1..12).
3. original: Python + Unicorn executes the ORIGINAL native x64 code (memory capture of the loaded EX5) starting at the native queue function. Terminal APIs are hooked and answered from api-fixtures.bin; native call order/arguments are checked against those records; it writes original-results.bin.
4. compare: byte-for-byte per-case comparison -> comparison.json.

Python class chain on the native side (modules loaded by path; dense code, many statements per line separated by ';'):
  kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh-bot-1-3.py : class Original(queue.Original)   <- main harness under review
  kiem-hang-doi-bot-1-3.py       : class Original(errors.Original)  (queue harness; its cases() are reused)
  kiem-chuoi-loi-bot-1-3.py      : class Original(send.Original)    (error-text helper)
  kiem-gui-lenh-bot-1-3.py       : class Original(pending.fill.entry.Original) (send wrapper/messages; Reader, populate, struct_bytes, supply, next)
  kiem-gia-vao-bot-1-3.py        : class Original(price_check.Original) (string(), alloc/free api 100/101)
  kiem-muc-gia-bot-1-3.py        : class Original (loads capture regions into Unicorn, base APIs 1,2,3)
Helper modules used but NOT in the MRO: kiem-tao-yeu-cau-cho-bot-1-3.py (pending: CFG, FIELDS, base(), Original.state_bytes called as an unbound function), kiem-kieu-khop-lenh-bot-1-3.py (fill: CFG), kiem-khoi-luong-hop-le-bot-1-3.py (original_hash).

Native RVAs (bot1 / bot3): queue 0x2e6d0 / 0x3bb10; pending builder 0x32dd0 / 0x3e580; filling 0x231c0 / 0x2e8f0; send wrapper 0x950 (both); error-text helper 0x336d0 / 0x3ee80; message functions bot1 0x235c0,0x23fa0,0x26060,0x26360 / bot3 0x2ecf0,0x2f6d0,0x31790,0x31a90. Builder return sites inside the queue are in RETURNS in kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh-bot-1-3.py.

FILES (R = ${R}):
  C:\\Users\\NTD\\Desktop\\Bot Market Demo\\AGENTS.md (project rules)
  R\\PHAN-TICH-CHUOI-DAT-LENH-BOT-1-3.md (owner's design claims for this harness)
  R\\cong-cu\\kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh-bot-1-3.py, kiem-hang-doi-bot-1-3.py, kiem-gui-lenh-bot-1-3.py, kiem-chuoi-loi-bot-1-3.py, kiem-tao-yeu-cau-cho-bot-1-3.py, kiem-kieu-khop-lenh-bot-1-3.py, kiem-gia-vao-bot-1-3.py, kiem-muc-gia-bot-1-3.py, kiem-khoi-luong-hop-le-bot-1-3.py
  R\\bot-cua-toi-1\\source\\MQL5\\Scripts\\bot-cua-toi-1\\Bot1PipelineApi.mqh and Bot1PendingPipelineCheck.mq5
  R\\bot-cua-toi-1\\source\\MQL5\\Include\\bot-cua-toi-1\\Bot1PendingQueue.mqh, Bot1PendingRequest.mqh, Bot1Filling.mqh, Bot1TradeSend.mqh, Bot1TradeMessages.mqh, Bot1TradeErrors.mqh
  (same file names with 3 instead of 1 under R\\bot-cua-toi-3\\...)
  Evidence: R\\bot-cua-toi-{1,3}\\bang-chung\\kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh\\pipeline-20261024-r1\\{comparison.json, baseline.json, mql5-run.json, original-run.json}
  Build receipts: R\\bot-cua-toi-{1,3}\\bang-chung\\bien-dich\\b{1,3}-pending-pipeline-01\\bien-nhan.json (+ metaeditor.log)
  Struct layout used by the native side: R\\doi-chung-mt5\\thu-tu-truong-lenh-class-20261024\\layout-class-r1\\trade-layout.json
  Capture metadata: R\\bot-cua-toi-{1,3}\\bang-chung\\captures\\luot-20261023-r1\\capture.json and R\\bot-cua-toi-{1,3}\\bang-chung\\luot-20261023-r1\\*.json
  Decompiled native C (large, Grep only): R\\bot-cua-toi-1\\phan-tich\\luot-20261023-data-v2\\ma-trung-gian.c (functions are named FUN_<hex absolute address>; bot1 image base 0x23e5aa10000, so the builder is FUN_23e5aa42dd0); R\\bot-cua-toi-3\\phan-tich\\luot-20261023-data\\ma-trung-gian-day-du.c (bot3 base = largest 'executable' region base in bot 3 capture.json).
`

const DIMENSIONS = [
  {
    key: 'execution-and-frame',
    prompt: `DIMENSION: real execution and builder-frame tracking.
Questions:
(1) In the native run of kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh-bot-1-3.py, do the original pending builder, the filling check, the send wrapper 0x950 and the message functions really execute instruction by instruction, or is there any remaining place where a whole function's result (especially the builder's bool or its request/result/check state) is supplied or short-circuited? Look for: ret stubs (b'\\xc3') written at non-terminal addresses, emu_stop hooks (e.g. before_send in kiem-tao-yeu-cau-cho), RIP/RSP rewrites, the old api 50 path in kiem-hang-doi, the address ranges allowed by visit. Trace hook registration and dispatch through the MRO: which call/visit/write_guard actually run for each hooked address, what self.apis maps each address to after every __init__ has run, and which addresses received b'\\xc3'.
(2) Is the builder-return detection sound (saved return address AND RSP == entry RSP + 8, checked in visit)? Could an inner ret, a tail call, recursion/re-entry, a jump to the return address, or Unicorn hook ordering cause a wrong or missed detection? What happens if the builder never returns or returns elsewhere?
(3) MQL5 side: does Bot{N}PendingPipelineCheck.mq5 run the real restored Bot{N}OpenPending / PreparePendingRequest / CheckFilling / SendTrade / message functions? Which identifiers are macro-replaced in which files? Check the #define/#undef scopes and include-guard order carefully, including whether the GetLastError/Print/Sleep/Bot{N}OpenPending macros leak into builder/send code or miss code they should cover.
Answer each question directly with evidence, then list findings.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'comparison-completeness',
    prompt: `DIMENSION: completeness and strength of every comparison.
Enumerate precisely what is compared, where and how:
(a) Per builder call, before and after (fixture events 10 and 11): which bytes/fields. Confirm whether all 35 request/result/check fields + magic + preferred + 4 full UTF-16 strings are compared. Check the native serialization (pending Original.state_bytes + strings() in kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh) against MQL5 WriteTradeState/WriteRequest/WriteResult field by field and offset by offset using trade-layout.json.
(b) Per case end (mql5-results.bin vs original-results.bin): queue trace events, all 500 doubles of the two tables, flag/counter/last error/sends/sleeps/prints, context, strings, final trade record, trailing counters. Check that writer (MQL5 WriteState etc.) and native serializer (kiem-hang-doi run + kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh run) are field-for-field symmetric.
(c) Every mocked terminal API (events 1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9): is the order, API kind, every argument, its type tag and the argument COUNT compared? Look for truncation or prefix comparisons, values the native side copies from the fixture instead of computing (tautological result fields), masks hiding bits, low-byte-only comparisons, result fields written from inputs instead of read from native memory.
(d) The 628-byte storage checks for stopped / non-stopped builder branches: what exactly do they prove, and on which builder calls are they meaningful?
For each weakness give path:line and say whether it can let a real divergence pass as a match (false match) or can only cause a false failure.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'oracle-and-timing',
    prompt: `DIMENSION: independence of the oracle, and timing/state across calls.
(1) List every value the native emulator consumes that was produced by the new MQL5 run (api-fixtures.bin events 1..12 and its chart/_Digits header) or that is hard-coded in the harness. Classify each as (i) a legitimate terminal/API input (OrderSend outcome, symbol property, number/string formatting, int-to-string cast, IsStopped flag, Sleep, memset...), (ii) a comparison target only (checked, never fed back), or (iii) an algorithm answer fed to the original code (circular). For (i), say whether the supplied value is cross-checked against cases.bin (replies, prep fields) or simply trusted from the MQL5 mock, and whether that matters.
(2) Timing: is the send error written to the native _LastError exactly when the native send API returns, matching MQL5 PipelineSendComplete? Is the property error written only when the reference-form SymbolInfoInteger returns false, on both sides? What about the direct long-returning form? Are queue-data mutations (queue patch / MQL5 ApplyBoundaryChange) applied only after the builder returns on both sides, and are Print/Sleep mutations triggered only by the queue's own Print/Sleep (not builder/send messages)?
(3) Multi-call state: retries and multi-order cases. Check counters (sends/sleeps/prints, reply index, actual sends), property-index resets per builder call, the per-call casts and per-case signed casts, request/result/check/magic/preferred carried between calls, initialize_trade once per case, and anything reset at the wrong time or lost between calls on either side, and between cases (MQL5 script globals, Python attributes, emulator memory/heap/cursor).`,
  },
  {
    key: 'evidence-and-coverage',
    prompt: `DIMENSION: evidence chain and coverage.
(1) Evidence chain from sources -> build receipt -> compiled .ex5 -> MT5 run -> api-fixtures/mql5-results -> native run -> comparison.json: what is hashed and re-verified in each mode (prepare/mql5/original/compare), and what is NOT pinned (imported Python modules, trade-layout.json, capture regions/capture.json/engine-observed.json, import.json metadata, CPU NaN reference, MT5 terminal build, the hand-written include list). How is the captured native image linked to the original EX5 SHA-256? Compare the hashes in the bot1 and bot3 comparison.json / mql5-run.json / original-run.json / baseline.json and explain what that implies. Is the tool_sha256 check sufficient?
(2) Coverage: from cases() in kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh-bot-1-3.py (plus kiem-hang-doi cases(), kiem-gui-lenh base(), kiem-tao-yeu-cau-cho base()), count the case groups and determine which branches of the restored MQL5 (Bot{N}PendingRequest.mqh, Bot{N}Filling.mqh, Bot{N}TradeSend.mqh, Bot{N}TradeMessages.mqh, Bot{N}PendingQueue.mqh, Bot{N}TradeErrors.mqh) these 818 cases can reach and which they cannot (examples to consider: NULL symbol, request actions other than 5, retcode values, stale last-error paths across orders, property values changing between retries, failing direct-form property reads, allocation failure, unknown expiration type).
(3) Unicorn NaN-payload correction scope: kiem-hang-doi patches addsd/subsd/mulsd only inside the queue function range. Check (Grep the decompiled C for the builder/filling/send/message functions, or reason from the MQL5 source) whether those other ranges contain floating-point arithmetic that could receive two NaN operands in these cases.
(4) Any statement in PHAN-TICH-CHUOI-DAT-LENH-BOT-1-3.md or in the comparison 'scope' text that overstates or contradicts what the code/evidence shows.`,
  },
]

const FINDINGS = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    answers: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      question: { type: 'string' }, answer: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    }, required: ['question', 'answer', 'evidence'] } },
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' },
      category: { type: 'string', enum: ['defect', 'weakness', 'limitation', 'observation'] },
      title: { type: 'string' },
      claim: { type: 'string' },
      evidence: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
      false_match_possible: { type: 'boolean' },
      impact: { type: 'string' },
      how_to_check: { type: 'string' },
      confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
    }, required: ['id', 'category', 'title', 'claim', 'evidence', 'false_match_possible', 'impact', 'how_to_check', 'confidence'] } },
  },
  required: ['answers', 'findings'],
}

const VERDICTS = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    verdicts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' },
      verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['confirmed', 'partly', 'refuted', 'unverifiable'] },
      reasoning: { type: 'string' },
      evidence: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
      corrected_claim: { type: 'string' },
    }, required: ['id', 'verdict', 'reasoning', 'evidence', 'corrected_claim'] } },
  },
  required: ['verdicts'],
}

const verifyPrompt = (label, claimsJson) => `${CONTEXT}
TASK: adversarial verification. Below are claims about the harness from "${label}". For EACH claim, try hard to REFUTE it by re-reading the cited lines and the surrounding code (including callers, overrides in subclasses, MQL5 counterparts and include/macro scopes). Verdicts: "confirmed" (the claim holds exactly as stated), "partly" (holds only with corrections — give the corrected claim), "refuted" (wrong — explain with evidence), "unverifiable" (cannot be decided from the files without running code — say what would decide it). Be strict about severity words: a check that can only produce false failures is not a false-match risk; a theoretical gap not reachable with the current code/cases must be labeled as such. Cite path:line for every verdict.

CLAIMS (JSON):
${claimsJson}`

const LEAD_CANDIDATES = [
  { id: 'L1', claim: 'Builder-frame Print argument COUNT is not compared: kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh-bot-1-3.py:243-248 builds `actual` from the native R8 count and compares with list(expected[:count]); if native passes fewer string args than the MQL5 MockPrint recorded (MQL5 uses a 2-argument Print at Bot1PendingRequest.mqh:38 / Bot3PendingRequest.mqh:38), the check still passes. fixtures() api 7 (lines 122-125) records the MQL5 count but it is never compared.' },
  { id: 'L2', claim: 'print_hash in the native result is taken from the MQL5-recorded output (kiem-gui-lenh-bot-1-3.py:273-277 `fmt,request,result,output=self.next(6)` ... `self.print_hash=text_hash(output)`), so the final print_hash equality is implied by argument equality and is not independent evidence. Likewise self.position written at kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh:258 equals len(records) by construction (257), so it always equals the MQL5 event_count.' },
  { id: 'L3', claim: 'original-run.json tool_sha256 pins only kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh-bot-1-3.py (line 301, checked at 309). The native logic in the imported modules (kiem-hang-doi, kiem-chuoi-loi, kiem-gui-lenh, kiem-tao-yeu-cau-cho, kiem-kieu-khop-lenh, kiem-gia-vao, kiem-muc-gia, kiem-khoi-luong-hop-le), trade-layout.json itself, import.json and capture.json/engine-observed.json are not hashed into baseline.json / original-run.json / comparison.json, so later changes to them are not detected by compare.' },
  { id: 'L4', claim: 'Symbol-property values/ok (events 2 and 9) fed to the native come from api-fixtures.bin produced by the MQL5 mock and are not cross-checked against the cases.bin prep fields (unlike kiem-tao-yeu-cau-cho-bot-1-3.py:111-127 which takes them from the case row). The send accepted flag IS cross-checked against queue replies (kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh:226). This is input-oracle trust, not output circularity.' },
  { id: 'L5', claim: 'The direct (long-returning) SymbolInfoInteger form (api kind 3 remapped to 47, fixture event 9) never sets _LastError on either side (kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh:235-238; Bot1PipelineApi.mqh:83-93), so a failing direct property read with an error code is not modeled or tested.' },
  { id: 'L6', claim: 'The Unicorn NaN-payload correction is installed only for addsd/subsd/mulsd inside the queue function range (kiem-hang-doi:151-161); builder/filling/send/message ranges added by the pipeline (kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh:163-166) run with Unicorn default NaN propagation. Whether this matters depends on whether those functions do FP arithmetic on two NaN operands.' },
  { id: 'L7', claim: 'The "reserved storage cleared" check (kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh:198-200) is only meaningful on the first builder call of each case, because the 0x5a fill (line 179) happens once per case in initialize_trade (triggered once at line 190).' },
  { id: 'L8', claim: 'kiem-hang-doi-bot-1-3.py:257 writes row["magic"] and row["virtual"] (inputs) into the native result instead of reading them from native memory; a native write to those globals would be caught only by the write guard, not by the comparison.' },
  { id: 'L9', claim: 'Unsigned-cast answers are dispatched by VALUE (kiem-gui-lenh:281-285) using harness-set request={"action":5,"type":type_}, result={"retcode":0} (kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh:219) and MQL5 hard-coded "5"/"0" strings (Bot1PendingPipelineCheck.mq5:93), so the test cannot tell which field the native cast when values coincide.' },
  { id: 'L10', claim: 'Coverage gaps in the 818 cases: symbol_null is always 0 and the queue symbol is always a non-NULL descriptor; request.action at send time is always 5 so message functions only exercise the pending branch; new_result.retcode takes only 6 values; no stale-132 path (accepted send leaving last error 132, then a later builder call failing before send); property values are identical on every retry because mock indexes reset per builder call (Bot1PendingPipelineCheck.mq5:100).' },
  { id: 'L11', claim: 'Bot 1 and bot 3 comparison.json show identical hashes for cases.bin, original-results.bin, mql5-results.bin, api-fixtures.bin and script-status.bin: consistent with identical behaviour of both bots on these cases, but the bot 3 run adds no observable data beyond confirming that identity.' },
  { id: 'L12', claim: 'self.records[self.position] at kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh:225 and :230 indexes without a bounds check, giving IndexError instead of a clean EXTRA_NATIVE_API error (robustness only; still fails loudly).' },
  { id: 'L13', claim: 'Return detection is sound against inner returns: visit (kiem-chuoi-dat-lenh:191) requires address == saved return AND RSP == entry RSP + 8; the entry hook (209-221) requires the return target to be one of RETURNS; nested entry raises (211); an unreturned frame raises (257).' },
  { id: 'L14', claim: 'In mql5 mode the source files are hashed before the MT5 run but not re-checked after it (only the binary at line 292); compare mode re-checks the current sources (305-306), so a change between run and compare is caught but a change during the run is not separately recorded.' },
  { id: 'L15', claim: 'The MT5 terminal build that produced the measured DoubleToString/StringFormat/cast outputs is not recorded in mql5-run.json, so the formatting oracle is not pinned to a terminal version.' },
  { id: 'L16', claim: 'PHAN-TICH-CHUOI-DAT-LENH-BOT-1-3.md:37 says "Chưa có kết quả chạy" but both comparison.json files exist with 818/818 matched, so the analysis document is stale relative to the evidence.' },
]

phase('Review')
const reviews = pipeline(
  DIMENSIONS,
  d => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n${d.prompt}\n\nReturn structured output: answers[] (one per question, with evidence) and findings[] (defects/weaknesses/limitations/observations, each with path:line evidence, whether a false match is possible, impact, how to check).`,
    { label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS, effort: 'max' }),
  (review, d) => {
    if (!review) return null
    const claims = (review.findings || []).map(f => ({ id: f.id, category: f.category, title: f.title, claim: f.claim, evidence: f.evidence, false_match_possible: f.false_match_possible }))
    if (!claims.length) return { dimension: d.key, review, verdicts: { verdicts: [] } }
    return agent(verifyPrompt(`reviewer ${d.key}`, JSON.stringify(claims, null, 1)),
      { label: `verify:${d.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICTS, effort: 'max' })
      .then(v => ({ dimension: d.key, review, verdicts: v }))
  },
)
const lead = agent(verifyPrompt('the lead reviewer', JSON.stringify(LEAD_CANDIDATES, null, 1)),
  { label: 'verify:lead-candidates', phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICTS, effort: 'max' })

const [dimensionResults, leadVerdicts] = await Promise.all([reviews, lead])
return { dimensions: dimensionResults.filter(Boolean), lead: leadVerdicts }

result: 5 agent đang chạy nền (đọc-chỉ, không chạy shell/MT5). Khi có kết quả, tôi sẽ đối chiếu lại từng nhận xét với mã trước khi báo.
